policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'Kittim' does not distinguish the qere כִּתִּים from the ketiv כתיים; no mapped textual note decides the spelling, so both readings remain compatible and the base fallback is retained.

ASV 'their towers' does not distinguish the qere בַחוּנָיו from the ketiv בחיניו; the mapped notes are alternative_rendering notes and therefore do not decide the reading, so both remain compatible and the base fallback is retained.
